keywords.def: coming from nature; developed without special training
designed and used for one particular purpose
involve someone or something, sometimes against their will
in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看BBC英语教学的6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Becca. And I'm Georgie. Remember, you can find all this episode's vocabulary along with a transcript and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我是Becca。我是Georgie。记住，你可以在我们的网站bbclearningenglish.com上找到本期节目的所有词汇、文稿和练习题。

sentences.en: Now, Becca, do you read a lot? Hmm, I don't read often.
sentences.zh: 那么，Becca，你经常读书吗？嗯，我读书不勤。

sentences.en: I just feel like I don't have the time, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我没有时间，Georgie。

sentences.en: How about yourself? I would love to read more, but I don't read very much at the moment.
sentences.zh: 你呢？我很想读更多书，但目前读得不多。

sentences.en: I read mostly before bed because I feel like it helps me relax and go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我主要在睡前阅读，因为我觉得这有助于我放松并入睡。

sentences.en: And today we're talking all about reading.
sentences.zh: 今天我们全篇都在讨论阅读。

sentences.en: We'll be hearing from some experts about how reading can change our brains, and as usual we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到一些专家关于阅读如何改变我们大脑的看法，像往常一样，我们还将学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: Let's start with a quiz question. The longest novel in the world is widely thought to be by French author Marcel Proust, a book which, when translated into English, means Remembrance of Things Past.
sentences.zh: 让我们从一个问答题开始。世界上最长的长篇小说普遍认为是法国作家马塞尔·普鲁斯特（Marcel Proust）的作品，这本书翻译成英文意思是《追忆似水年华》。

sentences.en: But how many words does the book contain?
sentences.zh: 但是这本书包含多少个词呢？

sentences.en: Is it: a) 130,000, b) 1.3 million, or c) 13 million?
OK. The longest novel in the world. I still think 13 million words sounds too many, so I'm going to go with b) 1.3 million.
sentences.zh: 好的。世界上最长的长篇小说。我还是觉得1300万个词听起来太多了，所以我选 b) 130万。

sentences.en: Alright. We'll find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, we might think of reading as like speaking.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可能会认为阅读就像说话一样。

sentences.en: We're born with the potential to do it and then we learn.
sentences.zh: 我们天生就有这样做的潜力，然后我们去学习。

sentences.en: It's natural. If something is natural, it's something you were born with or that comes from nature.
sentences.zh: 这是自然的。如果某事是自然的，那就是你与生俱来的或是来自大自然的。

sentences.en: But Maryanne Wolf, author of the book Reader Come Home, says that this isn't true.
sentences.zh: 但《阅读，回到祖国吧》（Reader Come Home）一书的作者玛丽安娜·沃尔夫（Maryanne Wolf）表示，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: We think of language as natural, and reading is written language so it must be natural.
sentences.zh: 我们认为语言是自然的，而阅读是书面语言，所以它一定也是自然的。

sentences.en: But it isn't. It isn't natural at all. Scientific studies suggest that when we're born, our brains already have the networks that allow our eyes to see and our vocal cords to produce sounds, but not with the pathways we need to read.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。一点也不自然。科学研究表明，当我们出生时，我们的大脑已经有了允许眼睛看到东西和声带发出声音的网络，但并没有我们阅读所需的神经通路。

sentences.en: Let's hear more from psychologist and neuroscientist Rebecca Gotlieb, speaking to the BBC World Service.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听心理学家兼神经科学家丽贝卡·戈特利布（Rebecca Gotlieb）接受BBC世界频道采访时的更多言论。

sentences.en: And so, to build a reading brain network, we co-opt parts of the brain involved in vision and auditory processing, and language, and attention and affect.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了构建一个阅读大脑网络，我们借用了大脑中参与视觉、听觉处理、语言、注意力和情感的部分。

sentences.en: Reading is really a whole brain process.
sentences.zh: 阅读确实是一个全脑过程。

sentences.en: It involves activation in all four lobes of the cortex.
sentences.zh: 它涉及皮层所有四个叶的激活。

sentences.en: The process of developing a reading brain alters everything, from brain activity to brain structure and brain connectivity.
sentences.zh: 开发阅读大脑的过程改变了一切，从大脑活动到大脑结构和大脑连接。

sentences.en: The power of deep reading is really fundamental to our humanity.
sentences.zh: 深度阅读的力量对我们的人性至关重要。

sentences.en: When we read deeply, we change our brains and we change who we are.
sentences.zh: 当我们深入阅读时，我们改变了大脑，也改变了我们自己。

sentences.en: Rebecca says that our brains haven't evolved to include a dedicated reading brain.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡说，我们的大脑并未进化到包含一个专门的阅读大脑。

sentences.en: Dedicated here means designed and used for one particular purpose.
sentences.zh: 这里的“专门”是指为一个特定目的而设计和使用的。

sentences.en: So, because we don't have a part of the brain designed specifically for reading, when we learn to read, we co-opt other parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为我们大脑中没有专门为阅读设计的部分，当我们学习阅读时，我们便借用了大脑的其他部分。

sentences.en: Co-opt here means to include someone or something, often against their will.
sentences.zh: 这里的“借用”是指将某人或某物纳入其中，通常是违背他们的意愿。

sentences.en: Right. Learning to read means using lots of different parts of the brain that are designed for other things, and this changes our brain structure compared to someone who hasn't learned to read.
sentences.zh: 没错。学习阅读意味着使用大脑中许多为其他事情设计的不同部分，与没有学过阅读的人相比，这改变了我们的大脑结构。

sentences.en: And the language we read also shapes our brain.
sentences.zh: 我们阅读的语言也在塑造我们的大脑。

sentences.en: Chinese characters, for example, use symbols instead of letters of the alphabet to represent words and ideas.
sentences.zh: 例如，汉字使用符号而不是字母表中的字母来代表单词和想法。

sentences.en: Research suggests that learning to read these symbols activates different areas of the brain to reading an alphabet-based system.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，学习阅读这些符号会激活大脑中与阅读基于字母的系统不同的区域。

sentences.en: Scientists studied a bilingual man who could read and speak Chinese and English.
sentences.zh: 科学家研究了一名能够阅读和说中文与英文的双语男子。

sentences.en: The man suffered a stroke, which affected parts of his brain, including his ability to read Chinese.
sentences.zh: 这名男子中风了，这影响了他大脑的一部分，包括他阅读中文的能力。

sentences.en: But amazingly, he was still able to read English.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊奇的是，他仍然能够阅读英文。

sentences.en: Maryanne Wolf explains more to the BBC World Service.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安娜·沃尔夫向BBC世界频道解释了更多。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful example of how the brain's circuit reflects the requirements of Chinese, which inevitably means more visual memory and visual processing of those beautifully intricate symbols or characters.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子，说明了大脑的电路如何反映中文的需求，这不可避免地意味着对这些精美复杂的符号或字符需要更多的视觉记忆和视觉处理。

sentences.en: Maryanne says that the brain's circuit is shaped by learning to read Chinese.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安娜说，大脑的电路是由学习阅读中文塑造的。

sentences.en: A circuit is a system of connections. The visual qualities of Chinese symbols inevitably mean more visual areas of the brain are developed.
sentences.zh: 电路是一个连接系统。中文符号的视觉特质不可避免地意味着大脑更多的视觉区域得到了发展。

sentences.en: Inevitably means in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地意为无法阻止或避免的方式。

sentences.en: Maryanne describes the symbolic Chinese characters as beautifully intricate.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安娜将象征性的汉字描述为精美复杂。

sentences.en: If something is intricate, it has lots of detail.
sentences.zh: 如果某事很复杂，它就有许多细节。

sentences.en: And something which also has lots of detail, or certainly lots of words – I asked you, Georgie, how many words are in Marcel Proust's Remembrance of Things Past.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事也有很多细节，或者至少有很多词——我问过你，Georgie，马塞尔·普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》里有多少个词。

sentences.en: I said 1.3 million. And you were correct!
sentences.zh: 我说130万。你猜对了！

sentences.en: Yay! The book also contains lots of very long sentences, including one with over 900 words.
sentences.zh: 耶！这本书还包含许多非常长的句子，其中有一个句子超过900个词。

sentences.en: One sentence with 900 words? That is a lot.
sentences.zh: 一个900个词的句子？那真是太多了。

sentences.en: OK. It's time to recap the language we learned during this programme, starting with natural, which describes something you were born with or that comes from nature.
sentences.zh: 好的。是时候回顾我们在本期节目中学习的语言了，首先是“自然的”（natural），它描述你与生俱来的或来自大自然的事物。

sentences.en: Dedicated can describe something that is designed and used for one particular purpose.
sentences.zh: “专门的”（dedicated）可以描述为某种特定目的设计和使用的东西。

sentences.en: If you co-opt someone or something, you involve them, sometimes against their will.
sentences.zh: 如果你“借用”（co-opt）某人或某物，你就会让他们参与进来，有时是违背他们的意愿的。

sentences.en: A circuit is a system of connections – for example, in the brain.
sentences.zh: 电路（circuit）是一个连接系统——例如在大脑中。

sentences.en: Inevitably means in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地（Inevitably）意味着以一种无法阻止或避免的方式。

sentences.en: And intricate describes something which has lots of detail.
sentences.zh: 而“复杂的”（intricate）描述了有很多细节的东西。

sentences.en: That's it for this episode of 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 本期6 Minute English节目就到这里。

sentences.en: Test what you've learnt with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 用我们网站bbclearningenglish.com上的练习题来测试你学到的知识吧。

sentences.en: Thanks for joining us. Goodbye! Bye.
sentences.zh: 感谢收看。再见！再见！
